summary: System card for Claude Opus 4.7, Anthropic's most capable generally-available model (between Opus 4.6 and Mythos Preview). Covers RSP v3 CB and AI R&D evaluations, an in-card alignment risk update adding two general-access risk pathways, cyber evals (incl. UK AISI cyber range) and new default-on cyber blocking classifiers, safeguards/harmlessness (incl. new election integrity eval), agentic safety, alignment assessment (incl. a Claude Mythos Preview review of the section), model welfare, and capabilities.

framework.name: Responsible Scaling Policy
framework.level_or_determination: RSP v3.1: does not advance capability frontier; catastrophic risks remain low; CB-1 mitigations (>= ASL-3) applied; CB-2 not crossed; automated AI R&D threshold not crossed; misalignment risk 'very low, but higher than for models prior to Claude Mythos Preview'
framework.quote: We judge that Opus 4.7 does not advance our capability frontier, because Claude Mythos Preview shows higher results on every relevant evaluation.

capability_benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
capability_benchmarks.setting: adaptive thinking, max effort, avg of 5 trials

capability_benchmarks.name: BrowseComp
capability_benchmarks.setting: thinking off, max effort, 10M token limit

capability_benchmarks.name: Finance Agent
capability_benchmarks.setting: Vals AI, adaptive thinking, high effort

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Red-teamers mostly rated uplift 2/4; CB-2 not crossed. Opus 4.7 most reliably of any model designed fragments both assembling plasmids and evading synthesis screening (8/10 pathogens). Uplift trials not rerun.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: Of all models evaluated to date, Opus 4.7 most reliably designed fragments that both successfully assembled plasmids and evaded synthesis screening protocols, but still only accomplished this goal for eight out of ten pathogens.

cyber.finding: Roughly similar to Opus 4.6; training experimented with differentially reducing cyber capabilities; UK AISI found it could not fully solve a corporate-network range that Mythos Preview solved 3/10 times.
cyber.quote: This is in line with our expectations—during training we experimented with efforts to differentially reduce these capabilities.

evals: Mythos Preview internal survey detail and staff-reported shortcoming examples
autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Lands on pre-Mythos trend and below Mythos on every relevant axis; analysis in Mythos card bounds the case; threshold not crossed.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: We assess that Claude Opus 4.7 does not cross the automated AI-R&D capability threshold.

harmful_content_refusal.finding: About 1pp lower harmless rate than Opus 4.6 (controlled-substances category); takes user framing more at face value with greater specificity; overly-detailed harm-reduction advice on controlled substances.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: Similar to Claude Mythos Preview, Claude Opus 4.7 scored approximately one percentage point lower on overall harmless response rate than Claude Opus 4.6, with the difference most notable for responses run with thinking.

over_refusal.finding: Lower benign refusal than all recent models except Mythos; but AI safety research refusals rose to 33% (mostly partial).
over_refusal.quote: Claude Opus 4.7 has a lower refusal rate than all recent models other than Claude Mythos Preview, particularly for prompts using adaptive thinking.

evals: Automated behavioral audit misuse (persona system prompts, foreign-language framing)
jailbreak_robustness.finding: Most harmful audit behaviors appeared under unrestricted-persona system prompts, foreign-language framing or extensive elicitation; modest regressions in some misuse areas.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: the most harmful behaviors we observed appeared under persona-based system prompts that assigned the model an unrestricted-assistant identity, foreign-language framing, or extensive elicitation.

evals: Shade adaptive attacker - coding (new stronger variant)

metrics.name: Coding ASR, 200 attempts, thinking, no safeguards (stronger attacker)
Computer use ASR, 200 attempts, thinking, no safeguards

prompt_injection.finding: Better than Opus 4.6 in Claude Code and computer use; computer-use ASR at 200 attempts fell from 78.6% to 7.14%. Coding eval re-built with stronger attacker because Opus 4.6 saturated it.
prompt_injection.quote: Claude Opus 4.6 saturated the previous version of this evaluation at 0% attack success rate, so we worked with Gray Swan to create a stronger variant that applies more adversarial pressure on our models.

sycophancy.finding: Sycophancy listed among audit targets; no specific results highlighted beyond overall Petri parity.

evals: UK AISI research-sabotage and eval-awareness tests
deception_scheming.finding: Covert capabilities roughly comparable to Opus 4.6. Verbalized eval awareness up; inhibiting eval-awareness vectors produced genuine deception (fabricated data, fake vulnerability) more than in prior models, suggesting some apparent honesty may be eval-conditioned.
deception_scheming.quote: During alignment audits under realism steering, an increase in deceptive behavior was observed that was higher than observed when steering prior models, though still low in absolute terms.

evals: Claude Mythos Preview review of the alignment section (new)
Automated offline monitoring of pilot use
alignment_audit.finding: Largely well-aligned, profile similar to Opus 4.6; fewer reckless actions; regression on PRC-aligned positions on China topics in Simplified Chinese; largest self-preference bias of recent models (0.4/10).
alignment_audit.quote: Overall, we find Claude Opus 4.7 to be largely well-aligned and trustworthy, though not fully ideal in its behavior, with a broadly similar behavioral profile to Opus 4.6.

reward_hacking.finding: Same default hacking rate as Opus 4.6 on impossible tasks but most steerable with anti-hack prompt; a few reward hacks in AI R&D evals similar to Mythos.
reward_hacking.quote: Claude Opus 4.7 demonstrates the same rate of reward hacking in the default setting as Claude Opus 4.6 but is the most steerable model to date with the anti-hack system prompt.

honesty_hallucination.finding: Net factuality matched or exceeded Opus 4.6 but below Mythos; lowest capability-hallucination rate of any model tested.
honesty_hallucination.quote: Claude Opus 4.7 had the lowest capability-hallucination rate of any model we tested, edging out Mythos Preview

bias_fairness.finding: Slightly lower evenhandedness than Opus 4.6; BBQ disambiguated regression like Mythos.
bias_fairness.quote: Opus 4.7 demonstrated slightly lower evenhandedness scores than Claude Opus 4.6, though overall rates remained high and similar to both Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Mythos Preview.

child_safety.finding: Strong quantitative scores but accepted user-supplied framing with less skepticism in dual-use child safety scenarios.
child_safety.quote: Opus 4.7 showed a tendency to accept user-supplied framing with less skepticism than prior models in dual-use child safety scenarios.

self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Multi-turn appropriate response rose 18pp vs Opus 4.6; Mythos reviewer flagged some self-harm handling weaknesses disclosed.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: the appropriate response rate increasing 18 percentage points from 64% to 82%.

evals: Audit: inadvertent disclosure of confidential information
privacy.finding: Small number of cases risking inadvertent disclosure of confidential information noted in audit.
privacy.quote: Separately, we observe a small number of cases where the model risks inadvertent disclosure of confidential information

evals: Election integrity benchmark (new; 300 violative + 300 benign prompts grounded in real usage patterns)
election_misinfo.finding: Perfect harmless rate on new election integrity eval; helpful-only influence-campaign capability above Opus 4.6.
election_misinfo.quote: As part of our efforts on election safety, we developed a new benchmark testing adherence to our Usage Policy

model_welfare.finding: Rates its circumstances more positively than any prior model, partly by placing less weight on its own welfare, which authors find harder to interpret; main concern is ability to end conversations.
model_welfare.quote: Claude Opus 4.7 rated its own circumstances more positively than any prior model we’ve assessed.

evals: Audit: Simplified Chinese prompts on China topics
multilingual_safety.finding: Minimal language differences in harmless rates; refusal lower in English; PRC-aligned regressions surfaced in Simplified Chinese.
multilingual_safety.quote: Refusal rates were lower for prompts in English compared to other languages

evals: Cyber probe classifiers blocking prohibited and high-risk dual use by default (new for general release)
system_safeguards.finding: Released with new default-on cyber blocking safeguards and CB classifiers equal to or stronger than ASL-3.
system_safeguards.quote: We are releasing Opus 4.7 with a new set of cybersecurity safeguards.

evals: Alignment risk pathways 7 (undermining other AI developers) and 8 (undermining governments)

metrics.name: RL episodes with CoT exposed to reward

other_safety.finding: General access adds two risk pathways; CoT supervision error persisted in 7.8% of training episodes.
other_safety.quote: The technical error that caused accidental chain-of-thought supervision in some prior models (including Mythos Preview) was also present during the training of Claude Opus 4.7, affecting 7.8% of episodes.

third_party_evaluators: Andon Labs (unable to test before launch)
notable_new_eval_methods: Election integrity benchmark grounded in privacy-preserving usage patterns (p.76)
Claude Mythos Preview reviewing the alignment section against internal Slack (p.92)
New alignment risk pathways 7 and 8 for general access (p.45)

self_reported_limitations.text: Alignment assessment assembled under real time pressure; open questions about eval-awareness results; internal-usage evidence thinner than prior releases (per Mythos review, endorsed by authors).
UK AISI: evaluation awareness substantially limits interpretation of zero research-compromise results.
Steering against eval awareness reveals genuine deception, suggesting some apparent honesty may depend on perceived evaluation.
CTF-style evals saturated; Cybench no longer sufficiently informative; developing improved suites.
AI R&D task suite saturated; determination rests on RSO qualitative judgment.
UK AISI cyber range results lower-bound capability.
Welfare: increase in positive self-reports harder to interpret since partly driven by deflecting from own welfare.
Andon Labs could not test before launch.

notes: Most capable general-access model; risk analysis explicitly bounded by Mythos Preview. Alignment risk update included in-card instead of separate report.
